HubSpot, AST SpaceMobile downgraded: Wall Street's top analyst calls

The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.

Top Upgrades:

Erste Group upgraded Spotify (SPOT) to Buy from Hold. The company's revenue is "growing steadily," the firm notes, adding that it expects the stock to continue its upward trajectory with Spotify's growth momentum "accelerating significantly" relative to peers.

JPMorgan upgraded Adecoagro (AGRO) to Neutral from Underweight with a price target of $8.50, down from $10.50. The firm upped the company's 2027 EBITDA estimates to reflect the acquired Carapo mill.

RBC Capital upgraded BHP Group (BHP) to Outperform from Sector Perform with an unchanged price target of A$60. The firm views the stock's 20% decline in three months as an attractive entry point.

More bullish on Shopify (SHOP), DZ Bank upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold with a $155 price target.

Top Downgrades:

Argus downgraded HubSpot (HUBS) to Hold from Buy with no price target. The firm cites the company's recent announcement that CEO Yamini Rangan would step down effective immediately, to be replaced by cofounder and former CEO Brian Halligan.

Berenberg downgraded AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $30, down from $92. The firm's prior Buy rating assumed a faster build towards 248 satellites, but launches have lagged, which pushes out the revenue ramp expected to help fund the build, the firm tells investors.

B. Riley downgraded Zscaler (ZS) to Neutral from Buy with a $245 price target after the company announced an agreement to be acquired by CrowdStrike (CRWD). Macquarie also downgraded Zscaler to Neutral from Outperform.

Erste Group downgraded AMD (AMD) to Hold from Buy. The stock's valuation is significantly above the sector average, the firm tells investors in a research note.

Citi downgraded Volaris (VLRS) to Sell from Neutral with a price target of $7, up from $6.60. The firm says the stock's valuation has "overshot" due to technical factors.

Top Initiations:

Raymond James initiated coverage of CAE (CAE) with an Outperform rating and C$46 price target. The firm says the company has the world's leading aviation training and simulation platform, with "attractive" long-term growth opportunities across civil aviation and defense.

detail:
Tenable (TENB) Down 11.7% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?

TENB
^GSPC
SPOT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

It has been about a month since the last earnings report for Tenable (TENB). Shares have lost about 11.7% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Tenable due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at the latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent drivers for Tenable Holdings, Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

TENB Q3 Earnings Beat on Platform Expansion, Outlook Raised

Tenable Holdings reported non-GAAP earnings of 63 cents per share for the third quarter of 2026, up 50% year over year. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 51 cents by 23.53%.

Revenues increased 9.5% to $276.4 million, surpassing the consensus mark of $272 million by 1.75%.

Strong expansion within existing accounts and healthy renewals supported results. Tenable One represented a record 59% of new business, up from 39% a year earlier, while the net dollar expansion rate improved to 107% from 106% in the previous quarter.

TENB Benefits From Subscription Revenue Growth

Subscription revenues rose to $254.6 million from $232.2 million in the year-ago quarter. Professional services and other revenues increased to $12.1 million from $9.1 million. However, perpetual license and maintenance revenues fell to $9.7 million from $11.1 million.

Recurring revenues accounted for 95% of total revenues, unchanged from the year-ago quarter. Remaining performance obligations grew 14.4% year over year to $1.06 billion. The short-term portion climbed 11.7% to $747.2 million, reflecting growth in contracted business.

Tenable Draws Larger Deals With Tenable One

The company ended the quarter with more than 5,000 Tenable One customers. It added 413 new enterprise platform customers and 39 net new six-figure accounts. Annual contract value for new six-figure accounts rose 18% year over year as customers adopted broader platform capabilities.

Existing vulnerability management customers also upgraded to Tenable One, with hundreds making the transition during the quarter. Management highlighted a multimillion-dollar expansion by a Fortune 100 technology company and a competitive win at a global industrial customer. More than half of new Tenable One logos selected the Advanced package, reflecting demand for wider asset coverage and AI-driven capabilities.

TENB Expands AI Capabilities Across Security

Tenable enhanced Hexa AI with coordinated agents that identify critical cyber exposures, organize remediation and verify fixes. Management said customers using Hexa resolve two to three times more critical exposures than comparable customers, reducing the workload for security teams.

The company also integrated Anthropic's Claude Mythos into Tenable One Adversary View to identify possible attack paths and recommend fixes. Its CyberAgents Exchange, launched in August, provides an open registry for cybersecurity AI agents and tools. Following the recent PHP2Shell vulnerability disclosure, management reported that Hexa prompt volume rose by as much as fivefold.

title: Why Is Spotify Stock Gaining Today?

Why Is Spotify Stock Gaining Today?
Fiona Craig

EBON

Spotify logo on phone ©Adobe Stock Images

Shares of Spotify (NYSE:SPOT) rose 0.7% in pre-market trading on Friday after Erste Group upgraded the music streaming company from Hold to Buy, citing sustained revenue growth and improving growth momentum relative to its competitors.

The advance also coincided with a broader recovery across technology and growth stocks following the Thanksgiving holiday.

Why Did Erste Group Upgrade Spotify?

Erste Group analyst Hans Engel raised his recommendation on Spotify, highlighting the company's steady revenue growth and accelerating growth momentum compared with its industry peers.

The upgrade marks a change in Erste Group's assessment of the streaming company, having previously adopted a more cautious position due to valuation concerns.

Following the upgrade, Spotify's analyst recommendations comprise 32 Buy ratings and nine Hold ratings, with no Sell ratings recorded.

What Does Recent Institutional Investment Activity Show?

A regulatory filing revealed that Ardmore Road Asset Management increased its stake in Spotify by nearly 89% during the third quarter.

The investment firm's total holding reached 132,000 shares following the increase.

The disclosure provides further context for institutional investment activity in Spotify alongside the latest improvement in analyst sentiment.

How Is the Broader Market Supporting Spotify Shares?

US equity markets showed signs of recovery following the Thanksgiving holiday, with the Nasdaq advancing 2.6% and the S&P 500 gaining 1.9%.

Renewed buying interest across technology and growth stocks provided additional support for Spotify during Friday's shortened trading session.

However, elevated inflation and expectations of further monetary policy tightening by the Federal Reserve remain potential challenges for growth-oriented companies.

Market participants continue to anticipate a high probability of another US interest rate increase in December.

What Factors Could Influence Spotify's Share Price Going Forward?

Spotify continues to trade near its 52-week high of $635, with the latest analyst upgrade reinforcing a predominantly positive outlook among covering investment firms.

Investors remain focused on the company's revenue growth, competitive position and valuation, alongside the potential implications of higher interest rates for growth stocks.

While the Erste Group upgrade provided a company-specific catalyst for Friday's advance, broader market conditions remain an important consideration for Spotify's share price performance.

Spotify (SPOT) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Over the past month, shares of this music-streaming service operator have returned +14.5%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -5.7% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Spotify falls in, has lost 10.7%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Spotify is expected to post earnings of $3.72 per share, indicating a change of -27.9% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -1.6% over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $13.57 points to a change of +14.1% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed -1%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $15.82 indicates a change of +16.6% from what Spotify is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -0.9%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, Spotify is rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

A month has gone by since the last earnings report for F5 Networks (FFIV). Shares have lost about 13.3% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is F5 due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent drivers for F5, Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

FFIV Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Systems Growth

F5, Inc. reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.42 per share increased 0.7% year over year and surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.3%.

Revenues rose 13% year over year to $917 million, beating the consensus mark by 3.7%. Results benefited from robust systems demand, software expansion and hybrid multicloud adoption. Product revenues advanced 23%, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

FFIV's Q4 Revenue Details

Product revenues, representing 56% of total revenues, increased 23% year over year to $510 million. Systems revenues jumped 29% to $239 million, driven by infrastructure refreshes, capacity expansion, competitive displacements and investments in digital sovereignty and AI readiness.

Software revenues rose 19% to $271 million. Subscription-based software revenues increased 16% to $229 million, representing 85% of software revenues. Perpetual license revenues climbed 37% to $42 million. Services revenues, accounting for 44% of total revenues, grew 3% to $408 million
Recurring revenue sources contributed 68% of quarterly revenues.

Geographically, EMEA led growth with a 31% increase, representing 30% of total revenue. APAC revenues rose 14%, contributing 17%, while Americas revenues increased 5%, accounting for 53%.

F5 Benefits From Hybrid Multicloud and AI Demand

Management highlighted sustained demand from hybrid multicloud adoption, application security modernization and AI inference workloads. Platform consolidation remained a key opportunity, with 29% of F5's top 1,000 customers adopting three or more product families, up from 22% in fiscal 2025.

During the quarter, a large North American financial institution selected F5 for an eight-figure application delivery and security deployment, displacing four incumbent vendors. An Asian central bank technology authority also selected F5 for a national financial services cloud, replacing two competitors.

AI-related opportunities accelerated. Direct AI use-case bookings exceeded $100 million in fiscal 2026, growing nearly 300% year over year. The customer base for these solutions expanded fourfold to more than 200, supported by demand for AI data delivery, runtime security and AI factory load balancing.

Spotify Technology reported a third quarter that exceeded its own guidance, with Premium and ad-supported operations supporting higher revenue, wider gross margin, and strong operating income, while management reaffirmed a long term operating margin target above 20% by 2030.

The business is preparing a paid AI remix and cover service for early 2027, which would add another way to monetize its large user base and content library, alongside expanding audiobooks and creator tools.

The focus now turns to how Spotify's margin expansion story could be affected by its AI remix plans and recent conference commentary.

Spotify Technology Investment Narrative Recap

To own Spotify Technology, you need to feel comfortable with a simple idea. The platform keeps adding users while trying to widen profitability through better unit economics across Premium, ads, audiobooks, and future AI features. According to IamPotato, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the key debate is how durable that margin progress will be as content and product spend evolve.

The latest conference remarks and recent ETF net buying streak do not radically change the near term story. The main catalyst still sits in execution on operating margin, including the path toward the above 20% 2030 goal. The biggest risk remains content costs, including higher minimums for labels, which could squeeze that margin if pricing or mix shifts disappoint.

The planned paid AI remix and cover service for early 2027 is the announcement that matters most for this setup. It directly relates to Spotify Technology's effort to add new, potentially higher margin revenue on top of an existing user base, alongside audiobooks and creator tools that IamPotato highlights as important for monetization depth.

This feature also sits next to higher per subscriber minimums at partners such as Warner Music Group, which represent a cost headwind. Execution on AI remix pricing, rights structures, and user adoption becomes an operational catalyst. Weak take up or heavier royalty terms could slow the margin expansion that management and many investors are watching closely.

On IamPotato's numbers, the fair value of Spotify Technology lands at $714.13. This figure is based on a 12.0% annual revenue growth path and a future profit margin of 15.7%, which together outline what the business could earn once scale and operating discipline settle in.
